title: How does a lift in a mine add and take away levels?
description: A lift runs in a mineshaft with levels in metres above and below the ground. Four problems are solved by starting at a level and moving the lift, using starting level plus movement and target level take away starting level. Keeko's doubt is that two moves below the ground are found by taking the smaller number from the larger.
teaching_notes: One idea: in the mine, two moves down add up their depths, and the movement needed is the target level take away the starting level. Watch for students who take the smaller number from the larger when both numbers are below the ground.

source: In the mine, levels above the ground are positive and below
video_script.why: The child uses the mine lift to add and take away levels given in metres, above and below the ground.
video_script.substitution: The four sums of the book's mine: positive forty plus positive sixty, negative ninety plus negative fifty five, positive forty take away negative fifty and negative ninety take away positive forty.
video_script.anchor: the lift in the book's mineshaft with levels in metres
video_script.wrong_move: takes the smaller number from the larger when both moves are below the ground
video_script.payoff_line: The answers are positive one hundred, negative one hundred forty five, positive ninety and negative one hundred thirty.

final_answer.spoken: positive one hundred, negative one hundred forty five, positive ninety and negative one hundred thirty metres

names.{{NAME_10}}: the building with floors above and below the ground

maths_rules: target level - starting level = movement needed
slip: 90 - 55 = 35 takes the smaller from the larger, but both moves go down so the depths add
video_script.design: One mineshaft drawn with ground level zero, four problems solved one after another with arrows.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a mine with a truck at ground level and a lift in the mineshaft

marks.scene: the title card arrives and the mine is drawn
marks.lift: the lift moves in the shaft and the truck waits at the ground
marks.levels: levels above the ground are marked positive and levels below negative, in metres
marks.ask: the lift stands at ground level with a question mark 50 m below

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a mine.
<bookmark mark='lift'/>A fast lift runs in the mineshaft, and the truck waits at ground level.
<bookmark mark='levels'/>Levels above the ground are positive, and levels below the ground are negative, in metres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The lift starts at ground level and goes down fifty metres. Which level does it reach?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: ground level 0; Starting level + Movement = Target level; Target level - Starting level = Movement needed

marks.zero: the ground level is marked 0 on the shaft
marks.rule: the line Starting level + Movement = Target level is written
marks.need: the line Target level - Starting level = Movement needed is written

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Ground level is zero. Each other level tells how many metres it is from the ground.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>As in the lift of {{NAME_10}}, the starting level plus the movement gives the target level.
<bookmark mark='need'/>Then the movement needed is the target level take away the starting level.

marks.list: the first two problems light up, then the last two

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four problems about the mine, with levels in metres.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Positive forty plus positive sixty, and negative ninety plus negative fifty five.
Then positive forty take away negative fifty, and negative ninety take away positive forty.

beats.on_screen: To find: the value of each

marks.find: the words value of each are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the value of each of the four.

marks.m1: the lift rises 60 m from level +40 and +100 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s1'/>Step one, positive forty plus positive sixty is starting level plus movement.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>The lift starts at level forty and moves sixty metres up, to level one hundred.

beats.on_screen: (-90) + (-55): start at -90, move 55 m further down; 90 + 55 = 145, so -145

marks.m2: the lift sinks 55 m further from level -90

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, negative ninety plus negative fifty five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The lift starts ninety metres below the ground and moves fifty five metres further down.
<bookmark mark='m2b'/>The depths add up, so it reaches level negative one hundred forty five.

beats.on_screen: (+40) - (-50): target +40, start -50; 50 up to 0, then 40 more = +90

marks.s3: the problem (+40) - (-50) is written as target level take away starting level
marks.m3b: the lift climbs 50 m to the ground and then 40 m more, and +90 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, positive forty take away negative fifty. This is target level take away starting level.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The lift starts fifty metres below the ground and must reach level forty.
<bookmark mark='m3b'/>It climbs fifty metres to the ground, then forty more, so ninety metres up.

beats.on_screen: (-90) - (+40): target -90, start +40; 40 down to 0, then 90 more = -130

marks.s4: the problem (-90) - (+40) is written as target level take away starting level
marks.m4b: the lift drops 40 m to the ground and then 90 m more, and -130 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, negative ninety take away positive forty. This is target level take away starting level.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The lift starts forty metres above the ground and must reach ninety metres below.
<bookmark mark='m4b'/>It drops forty metres to the ground, then ninety more, so one hundred thirty metres down.

marks.ans: the four results are boxed in a row
marks.unit: the unit m glows beside each result

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The answers are positive one hundred, negative one hundred forty five, positive ninety and negative one hundred thirty.
<bookmark mark='unit'/>All four are in metres.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: -35 crossed out; the shaft with two downward arrows, 90 m and 55 m, joined end to end

marks.fix: -35 is struck out and the two downward arrows join end to end
marks.sum: the total depth 145 m is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks negative ninety plus negative fifty five is negative thirty five, after taking fifty five from ninety.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But both moves go down, so the lift only gets deeper.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>The depths add up to one hundred forty five. The level is negative one hundred forty five.
